title: Auto Loans: Paying Off a Loan from PCB Checking
content:
An Auto Loans borrower at Piedmont Crescent Bank can close the loan by paying it off today from their own PCB checking account. This page describes the service and the action that posts it.

## Scope

A borrower who wants an auto loan settled in full today, with the money taken from a PCB checking account they own, is served by a single payment of the payoff kind. The agent posts it for the payoff amount, and today is its credit date.

## Business effect

The payment is booked on the loan's activity as a payoff made by PCB transfer, divided into its fees, interest and principal shares; a matching fee settlement is booked where the fees share is above zero. The loan's unpaid principal and unpaid fees become 0.00, today is recorded as both the last payment date and the closing date, the loan is marked paid off with no installment due and no days past due, and the lien release is marked as pending. The borrower then sees the loan as paid off.

## Using the action

The action `post_payoff_payment_63569e96` is an agent tool held back until unlocked; the agent unlocks it and makes the call.

| Parameter | Description | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_loan_id` | the loan to be closed, identified through the auto loan lookup | identifier |
| `amount` | the whole payoff payment drawn from checking | USD, two decimals |
| `fees_portion` | share of the payoff settling fees | USD, two decimals; 0.00 when no fees are due |
| `interest_portion` | share settling accrued interest | USD, two decimals |
| `principal_portion` | share settling principal | USD, two decimals |
| `counterparty_account_id` | the borrower's PCB checking account the payoff money comes out of, identified through the checking account lookup | identifier |

## Receipt

Success reads status "paid_off", with `payment_reference` (a 12-digit number identifying the payoff), `auto_txn_id` (the payoff entry), `fee_settlement_id` (the settlement booked for fees, or "" where the fees share is 0.00), `closed_date` (today) and `lien_status` ("release_pending").
